message.content:
Attack. Opus: “every historical onset came during an inversion or within 9 months of its end” and “the only way the memory question can ever be settled.” The first is false on the table in front of us. 1957, 1960 and 1990 had no ≥3-month inversion — 3 of 12 fit onsets. The 9-month figure is the maximum lag inside the inversion-associated subset, not a property of onsets. The second fails on power: MDE80 on a paired skill gap is ≈30 pp with 8 walk-forward onsets. Two post-sealing onsets, at ~1.5/decade, cannot settle a 30 pp gap. A monthly `p_hukommelse` through 2026–27 is a monitoring number beside a live P of 14.8%, which is the use this council refused yesterday.

Gemini: “the shadow model reads near P today (+0.24 vs +1.12), which proves we are not fitting to the current cycle.” No fit has been run, so “near P” is not a result. The operational slope is −1.2948 per pp. The gap they are dismissing is 0.88 pp. Substituting the min for the level moves the linear index by about 1.14 logits, from 14.8% to roughly 35%. A joint L2 fit will not do that substitution, but it also will not leave α and the curve slope unchanged: ridge on two collinear columns splits one signal. Closeness is unidentified until the fit, and fitting in order to confirm closeness before sealing is the fork. Choosing H=12 after E2 has shown H=24 at −0.41 and H=36 at −1.22 is conditioning on this cycle. It does not prove the opposite.

The scored-bar camp has not pinned a bar. Block length is 4 quarters (Gemini), mean 8 (Fable), 16 (Kimi), 20 (DeepSeek). Four SEs are four tests. §5.2 requires one numerically pinned symmetric bar before any run. With divergence concentrated in 2–4 quarters per cycle, a 16- or 20-quarter block after two onsets estimates SD from about two blocks. That threshold will not be a test.

Steelman. GPT, missed in my Round 1: a positive `curve_min12` does not imply the shadow probability is close to P, because the joint refit moves the intercept and both slopes. I struck the sales sentence and did not put the mechanism on the fallback. Fable’s companion point also stands: origins through 2025Q3 already carry resolved non-onset labels after the 2022–24 inversion, so a full-sample coefficient has partly seen the episode under debate.

Revised positions. Q1 unchanged: no shadow probability. Q2: still `curve_min12` only, and only as a state if anything is logged. I withdraw the pin “smallest multiple of 12 that covers the 9-month lag.” That rule was built after E1; H=9 would cover 9, and rounding to 12 is discretion. Pre-existence of the v4 object is the only tie-breaker against (b)–(d) and against H=24/36. It is contaminated by an unrecorded v4 result. It is not identification. Q3: still do not fit. Fallback, only if overruled: same change as Round 1, plus a once-printed coefficient vector on origins ≤2022Q3, training-only standardisation, and an explicit ban on claiming ex ante that the shadow reads near P. No pre-seal fit to inspect divergence. Q4 unchanged: no `p_*` field, not in `hovedbog.jsonl`, not in LOG.md, not on the dashboard. If a state is logged, `curve_min12` in percentage points, unscored. Q5 unchanged: this sitting seals no bar. Q6 unchanged: do not start a memory model in November 2026. At the 2026-09 input, `curve_min12` is +0.24. The inversion this item is about is already outside the window.

AGREE: nothing changes operational P or the frozen weights; one object only, no parallel candidates; reject H=24/36 and (b)–(d) under this mandate; `curve_min12` is the only memory variable anyone will accept; no dashboard probability; no automatic switch into P; any fit, if forced, uses λ=1, the operational universe, and must disclose E1–E4 contamination.
DISAGREE: shadow probability at all — Grok against the other six; fit now — same split; seal a 1.96·SD bar in this spec — Grok and GPT against Fable, Opus, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, who also disagree with each other on the block; November 2026 start — Grok against the other six; LOG.md after 2027 — Gemini and Kimi want a permanent ban, Opus and DeepSeek only defer it.
CHANGED-MY-MIND: withdrew the 9-month-covering pin for H=12; it was post hoc. Added, on the fallback only, the ≤2022Q3 disclosure vector and a ban on any ex ante closeness claim. Did not move on authorising a second P.
message.reasoning:
I am assuming the Grok 4.7 persona for this council response.

I will attack two other councillors with specific rejected claims and mechanistic evidence. I will identify the single best idea from another councillor that Round 1 missed. I will revise my positions where warranted. The response will end with three labeled lists: AGREE, DISAGREE, and CHANGED-MY-MIND. The word limit is about 800.

I will target Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable and Gemini for claiming the shadow settles the question or that H=12 matches E1. I will reject these with specific mechanisms rather than opinion.

Claude Opus 5.5's claim that a monthly shadow P settles the memory question is rejected with a concrete mechanism: an MDE80 of roughly 30 points and eight walk-forward onsets means two post-sealing onsets cannot close that gap. Claude Opus 5.5's Q2 assertion that every historical onset occurred during an inversion or within nine months of its end is also rejected, citing 1957, 1960, and 1990 as counterexamples. Gemini's argument that H=12 proves the shadow model reads near P today (+0.24 pp min versus +1.12 pp level) is targeted because that spread does not prove the current cycle is not being fit.

The H=12 argument is invalid because adding a correlated predictor shifts the intercept and both slopes, so a positive minimum does not imply the shadow equals P. The choice of H=12 was also selected on the known consequence that H=12 is silent while H=24 and H=36 light up. Kimi’s bootstrap with 16-quarter blocks and 1.96 standard deviations after only two onsets is underpowered, and the bar remains unidentified. DeepSeek repeats the same error as Gemini and Claude. GPT’s private companion ledger is noted as an interesting development.

I am now searching for the single best idea from another councillor that Round 1 missed. Claude Fable’s framing of the shadow as a pre-registration of a falsifiable number rather than a test with usable power is one candidate, though I still reject the probability field itself. GPT’s sharper correction on how adding a correlated predictor shifts intercept and slopes is another possibility. I am weighing which idea to adopt as my steelman.

Claude Fable’s proposal to log `curve_min12` itself every row is a useful addition, since it makes the record reconstructible without the model. Gemini’s live definition of the shadow as `min(C_live, min of preceding 11 calendar months)` is also a concrete implementation detail worth adopting if the state is logged.

Claude Fable’s structural pin that H equals the label horizon, independent of E2, is the best idea I missed. The operational sample already contains resolved zero labels for origins through 2025Q3 after the 2022–24 inversion, so the fit has partly seen the episode. GPT’s public hovedbog.jsonl point was already covered in Round 1.

I will not fold to the 6-1 majority. I am now cataloguing hits on my position to see if any revision is warranted.

Claude Fable’s point that prose context cannot be falsified is a concrete hit on the probability field. A logged curve_min12 is a verifiable number, whereas a probability is an unidentified transformation of that same number.

GPT’s private archive versus public ledger distinction is also relevant: if hovedbog is public, logging curve_min12 directly may suffice, since a spread is not a probability. The distribution argument was specifically about an alternative P.

My Q6 objection that November cannot record the 2022–24 inversion for H=12 remains a live issue.

The Q6 objection is confirmed: a 12-month horizon would indeed be blind if the 2022–24 cycle ends in a 2027 recession, and Claude Opus 5.5 itself flags this as the biggest risk. No one successfully rebutted that mechanism.

Logging curve_min12 would not add new information, because the inversion note already records end date, depth, and lag versus historical max. That value is also publicly derivable from FRED.

I will hold my Round 1 position on Q1: no shadow probability.

I will not change my position on logging the raw feature. I will adopt Claude Fable’s disclosure requirement as a mandatory condition for any fallback fit, since resolved zeros through 2025Q3 already contaminate the sample. I had a fallback in Q3 but omitted the pre-2022Q3 coefficient vector.

DeepSeek’s argument that the shadow is acceptable despite post hoc motivation because it costs almost nothing is rejected. Creating a quotable second P does not cost nothing; it triggers the distribution mechanism from yesterday.

Gemini’s own risk section admits the 1.96 bar will not fire, so sealing it now is theater. I will quote Gemini against Gemini and Claude on this point.

The response will be concrete and quantitative, with no filler or hedging.

I will add the explicit sentence that H=12 was known to read near +0.24 into any sealed specification. I may also adopt Gemini’s live trailing-month aggregation as a specification improvement for the fallback, though this does not change my vote. I still reject Q1 and Q5.

I am now weighing whether to drop even the fallback logging of curve_min12. Fable’s point that a ledger field is a pre-committed timestamped number that cannot be rewritten after the outcome is compelling, but the inversion note already appears on the dashboard and is presumably versioned. I am deciding whether this justifies keeping the fallback or rejecting it entirely.

I will adopt the raw `curve_min12` as an append-only ledger field. This is a commitment device that cannot be rewritten after the outcome, and it does not require a probability. I will start logging this value in November because it is pre-defined and does not depend on a fit. My Q6 objection that H=12 has already forgotten the 2022–24 inversion remains valid.

Logging the raw curve_min12 every month does not resolve the Q6 objection, because a 12-month horizon remains blind to lags beyond nine months. The November start date is abandoned.

GPT’s correction that a joint refit shifts the intercept, slope, and lag simultaneously destroys the “shadow reads close to P” justification used by Opus, Fable-adjacent, Gemini, and DeepSeek. This is the steelman.

The GPT correction is reinforcing rather than a new reversal. The fallback specification will now require a disclosed coefficient vector for origins through 2022Q3 and explicitly state whether standardization uses population or sample variance, since Kimi specified population.

I will now accept GPT’s point that any shadow probability must live in a private companion ledger, not hovedbog.jsonl. This is a conditional concession on the storage rule.

I also corrected my own pin: H equals the smallest multiple of 12 covering the maximum inversion-end-to-onset lag in E1, which is 9 months, so H=12. I had wrongly claimed this covered all onsets; Fable and others noted that 1957, 1960, and 1990 had no inversion, so the pin only applies to inversion episodes.

The label-horizon argument is weaker than claimed. A 12-month backward window is not implied by a 4-quarter forward label; it is only a rhetorical match. I will keep the 9-month lag pin but disclose that the choice of H = 12 was made knowing E2 reads near +0.24.

I will drop the 9-month lag pin entirely. It is post hoc: the 12-month horizon was chosen after seeing the 9-month lag, and a 9-month horizon would have covered it just as well. If a state is logged, curve_min12 remains the only pre-existing object, so the 9-month story is not a valid pin. This corrects my own Q2.

The operational probability, weights, and curve-only lock remain untouched. H=24 and H=36 are rejected for this mandate, as are candidates (b), (c), and (d). The feature search stays closed to one object only. Pre-2027 contamination must be disclosed if any fallback fit is attempted. MDE80 is roughly 30 percentage points, yet two onsets is underpowered; several council members acknowledge this while still sealing a bar.

The council is split on three points. Grok alone wants to log a shadow probability and fit coefficients now; the other six reject both. On the 1.96·SD scored bar, Grok and GPT are in favor while Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, Fable, and Opus oppose it. Fable wants a specified bar; the others want variants.

GPT supports unscored tracking but not a formal superiority test under this specification. The council is split on three additional points: Grok rejects November as the start date for a memory model, while others accept it; Gemini and Kimi want LOG.md permanently excluded after 2027, whereas Opus and DeepSeek say not before the next refit; GPT, Grok, and Kimi deny that the shadow will read near P, while Gemini, DeepSeek, and Opus assert it will.

The council’s “yes bar” camp is internally split. Gemini proposes a 4-quarter block, Kimi 16, DeepSeek 20, and Fable a stationary mean block of 8. §5.2 requires one numerically pinned symmetric bar before any run, so the council has not pinned a single bar.

Opus’s claim that every historical onset occurred during an inversion or within nine months of its end is falsified by three cases: 1957, 1960, and 1990-08 had no inversion at all. The nine-month maximum is therefore a property of inversion episodes that were followed by recessions, not a universal bound on onsets.

Gemini’s argument that the shadow reads near P because the fit avoids the current cycle is also flawed. A z-scored joint L2 penalty with high correlation between curve and memory causes ridge regression to split the coefficient β, so the shadow does not simply track the operational probability.

The shadow probability is logit⁻¹(α + β1 z_c + β2 z_m), so it cannot equal the operational P unless β2 is exactly zero. Without the fitted coefficient, the claim that the two probabilities read near each other is a numerical assertion with no number behind it.

Kimi’s argument that two onsets satisfy the eligibility minimum is weakened by Gemini’s own risk estimate: only about two to four quarters per cycle are informative divergence windows.

A 16-quarter block bootstrap from only two onsets yields just two effective independent blocks. The standard deviation is estimated from those same two episodes, so the 1.96·SD critical value is unidentified and cannot serve as a test. The bar disagreement will be folded into DISAGREE, with Opus and Gemini as the two required sides.

I will adopt a rule forbidding any fallback specification from claiming ex ante closeness between the shadow and operational probability. The GPT correction is the cleanest steelman because it directly challenges a claim repeated by four councillors. I will also invoke the distribution argument that Claude Opus is the interested party, ensuring he receives at least as hard scrutiny as the other sides.

The operational model with curve at +1.12 yields a probability of roughly 14.8%, confirming the 0.88 percentage point gap against the memory feature. This quantifies the numerical distance behind Gemini’s near-P claim.

A naive substitution of the memory feature at +0.24 into the operational model yields roughly 35%, not the 14.8% P, so the shadow cannot simply be read as a shifted version of the base probability. The real issue is that in-sample collinearity between curve and memory can make the partial coefficient on memory arbitrarily small, meaning today’s reading could sit near or far from P depending on the fit.

The near-P claim is a researcher-discretion fork: it can only be verified by running the fit before sealing. The 0.88 percentage point gap equals roughly 1.1 logits, or about 20 percentage points of probability, so “close to P” is not a mechanical implication of the memory feature alone. DeepSeek also asserts the shadow will read near P.

Kimi and GPT both correctly reject the near-P claim. I will stage three brief attacks to stay under 800 words. The Fable steelman is two-fold: log the raw feature value for reconstructibility, and disclose that the fit already sees resolved zeros after this inversion because origins extend through 2025Q3.

The Q3 fallback now requires a mandatory ≤2022Q3 disclosure vector and forbids any ex ante claim that the shadow probability equals the operational P. The fit must not be run to check divergence before sealing. Q1, Q4, Q5, and Q6 remain unchanged. I did not authorize a shadow probability. The pin and the disclosure vector are the sole changes.
